Opening cans that have to be peeled and then pop to open (Pillsbury cans for example). I don't like the popping noise and it's like holding a grenade to me. I always make someone else open them for me and then turn around so I don't have to watch them open it.
Drive throughs; I am perfectly fine going inside and ordering, but driving around the building and talking to some person in a box just freaks me out.

Chiping a tooth. Just the thought makes me cringe. It's like, that chip is gonna be there forever and I'm always gonna feel it with my tongue all the time.
Snakes. The snakes here are all non-poisonous...
Falling through a manhole cover or storm drain grate.

Sharp things sitting out. I have no problem using knives and whatnot, but once they're no longer being used, they should be put away! I'm not even afraid for myself. I just picture somebody else getting a bad cut.

Homelessness. I'm a disabled vet and it seems that I'm constantly seeing things about the disparity on the percent of homeless folk that are disabled vets. I doubt that this is a realistic risk for me, but it terrifies me.

Storms. It was actually bad enough that I'd go into blind panic attacks over them. Granted I've been through a couple of tornados which probably doesn't help. Went through cognitive behavioural therapy so that I wouldn't be affected at work (happened once last year when a microburst went over the mall, I had a very clear view from the windows above my kiosk and essentially curled up in a ball and cried). Doing much better now, I can actually stand out on a porch to watch the lightning.
